text:
Alex K: hey team — stuck on local compose + redis. my app container gets "NOAUTH Authentication required." when it talks to the redis service even though I set REDIS_PASSWORD in .env.
Maya S: do you have a custom redis.conf or using the official image? some images read env vars differently.
Alex K: default official redis: image: redis:6.2; compose has 
```yaml
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:6.2
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    environment:
      - REDIS_PASSWORD=${REDIS_PASSWORD}
```
I connect with redis-cli -h redis -a $REDIS_PASSWORD from the app but still NOAUTH.
Jordan P: official redis doesn't consume REDIS_PASSWORD env — it expects requirepass set in redis.conf or via command args. env var is ignored unless you're using a wrapper image.
Sam L: yep, either mount a redis.conf with requirepass, or start redis with `redis-server --requirepass "$REDIS_PASSWORD"`. on mac, host networking weirdness can also bite, but since you're connecting from another service, service name should work.
Alex K: ah ok. i tried adding command: ["redis-server", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"] and still saw errors. logs showed: 
```
1:C 23 Mar 2026 14:05:10.123 # WARNING: The TCP backlog setting of 511 cannot be enforced because /proc/sys/net/core/somaxconn is set to the lower value of 128.
1:M 23 Mar 2026 14:05:10.124 * Ready to accept connections
1:M 23 Mar 2026 14:05:12.456 - Accepted 172.18.0.4:34822
1:M 23 Mar 2026 14:05:12.457 # Client id=5 authentication failed.
```
Alex K: then redis-cli -h redis -a $REDIS_PASSWORD -p 6379 from app container still ERR invalid password
Maya S: are you sure the env var is populated inside the redis container? docker-compose variable expansion happens at compose parse time — but command: with ${REDIS_PASSWORD} is expanded on the host, not injected into container unless you export in env.
Jordan P: try putting the password into a file or volume so redis reads from redis.conf and confirm with `docker-compose exec redis env | grep REDIS`. also confirm your app isn't connecting before the password is set.
Alex K: good point — i did `docker-compose up -d` and env had REDIS_PASSWORD in .env. ran `docker-compose exec redis printenv | grep REDIS` and nothing printed.
InfraBot: container redis (id: a1b2c3d4) started 14:05:09, args: ["redis-server", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
Sam L: InfraBot shows literal ${REDIS_PASSWORD} — that means compose didn't expand it into the command array. Compose v2 treats command as a list and does not do variable expansion in some cases. Try passing the command as a single string or use entrypoint script that reads env.
Maya S: easiest fix: mount a redis.conf at /usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf with a line `requirepass your_password` (or use envsubst in a small init script). example: 
```yaml
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:6.2
    ports:
      - 6379:6379
    volumes:
      - ./redis.conf:/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf
    command: ["redis-server", "/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf"]
```
And in redis.conf: `requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD}` then use envsubst on startup.
Jordan P: or `command: sh -c "envsubst < /etc/redis/redis.conf.template > /etc/redis/redis.conf && redis-server /etc/redis/redis.conf"`
Alex K: ok i switched to the volume+envsubst pattern and it worked. verified with `docker-compose exec redis redis-cli -a $REDIS_PASSWORD ping` => PONG :+1:
Sam L: also FYI, for local dev you can set REDISCLI_AUTH in your app container so scripts using redis-cli don't need -a every time.
Alex K: thanks! saving this snippet in the repo.
Maya S: welcome aboard — feel free to ping if anything else blocks your setup :wave:
Alex K: much appreciated everyone, got back to the app tests passing.
InfraBot: note: please avoid committing secrets to repo; use .env.local and add to .gitignore.
